subject: general
question: Who is the highest executive officer in the country?
solution:
The correct answer is__** President.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The President is the head of the executive branch of the Indian government.**
 
• The President is elected by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both houses of Parliament and of the Legislative Assemblies of the States.
 
• **The President holds the power to appoint the Prime Minister, other ministers, judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts, and other key officials.**
 
• The President also has the power to promulgate ordinances when Parliament is not in session and to dissolve the Lok Sabha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Lok Sabha Speaker is the presiding officer of the Lok Sabha, which is the lower house of the Indian Parliament.**

 
 
• The Lok Sabha Speaker is responsible for maintaining order and decorum in the House and for conducting its business.
 
• The Lok Sabha Speaker is elected by the members of the Lok Sabha.
 
 
 
• **The Vice President is the second-highest constitutional post in India after the President.**
 
 
• The Vice President is elected by an electoral college consisting of the members of both houses of Parliament.
 
• The Vice President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, which is the upper house of the Indian Parliament.
 
 
 
• **The Prime Minister is the head of the Council of Ministers, which is the executive branch of the Indian government.**
 
 
• The Prime Minister is appointed by the President and is responsible for running the government and implementing its policies.
 
• The Prime Minister is accountable to the Lok Sabha, which can remove him/her through a vote of no-confidence.
